target_customer: Law firms and in-house legal teams, including large international firms
problem: Lawyers spend long hours on research, document review and drafting. Legora offers an AI workspace and agents to speed up complex legal workflows.
business_model: Enterprise B2B SaaS sold to law firms and legal departments

founders.name: Max Junestrand
education: Stockholm School of Economics, business degree
founders.background_notes: From the YC page bio: also worked in venture capital and as a software developer at Abios (later acquired by Kambi).

competitors.name: Casetext CoCounsel
competitors.what: GPT-4 based legal assistant for research and review
competitors.traction_then: Debuted March 2023, acquired by Thomson Reuters four months later
competitors.funding_then: Acquired for 650M USD (per a vendor blog)

competitors.name: Harvey
competitors.what: Generative AI assistant for large law firms
competitors.traction_then: Founding and launch details not found in the opened sources

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on third-party LLMs in 2023, so the hard parts were legal-quality retrieval, drafting workflows and enterprise security rather than model research. Legora later states it does not build its own model.

defensibility.rationale: Law firm workflow integration, security approvals and customer relationships create stickiness, but rivals Harvey and CoCounsel sell similar capabilities.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Thomson Reuters bought Casetext in 2023 and bundled CoCounsel with Westlaw. Legora was not acquired; it has instead become an acquirer, buying Walter, Qura, Graceview, Cadastral and Wexler in 2026.

market_need_then: Law firms had large document-heavy workloads and growing interest in GPT-4 after early 2023; Casetext's quick sale for 650M USD (per a vendor blog) showed willingness to pay.

branding.name_origin: Company name derives from Latin meaning roughly 'to bring things together', per rebrand coverage. The earlier name Leya was used until February 2025.
branding.domain_note: Operated Leya on a .law domain before the 2025 rebrand, then secured the exact match legora.com (2025-02).

identity.logo: New identity unveiled with the rebrand; details not retrieved

rebrands.why: Tied to European expansion and a more durable global identity with a .com domain, per coverage

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage of the rebrand by Artificial Lawyer, Law360 and Business Wire; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong enterprise recognition among large law firms and a successful rebrand to a .com name, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth beyond product and sales.

outcome_analysis: Legora, founded in 2023 as Leya and rebranded in February 2025, rode the generative AI wave into large law firms and raised seed, Series A to D and an extension between 2024 and 2026, with the YC page citing a 5.6B USD valuation and 200M USD plus ARR. Fast sales to big firms, repeated leading investors and a 2026 acquisition spree explain the growth. Harvey remains the main rival, and incumbents such as Thomson Reuters bundle competing tools.
notes: Series B figure (80M USD, 675M post-money, May 2025) is confirmed in the Series C Business Wire release text as per search summary; the valuation comes from an aggregator so basis is estimated. The series_d_plus 2026-03 round is reported by the YC description as 600M USD total including the 50M April extension, so the 550M plus 50M split matches. A later 550M round at 8.8B valuation labeled Series E appears in City AM and AI Magazine snippets with no date; the AI Magazine page returned 403 and was not worked around, so it is unverified and not recorded. Talks at 10B USD valuation were reported by Sifted. Haqq is a competitor-adjacent vendor blog so Casetext price is weak. Harvey founding info not found.
